headlines.title: Drake Maye likely done for the season
headlines.summary: Yahoo's Week 11 injury tracker lists Patriots quarterback Drake Maye as likely done for the season. The same update says Jordan Addison is having surgery. New England lost 35–10 to Detroit in Munich on Sunday, the game the Patriots played as part of their trip to Germany.
headlines.whyItMatters: New England is 5–5, eighth in the AFC and one game behind the seventh seed. Losing their starter for the rest of the year makes that climb much harder.

headlines.title: Bosa says he isn't playing his best
headlines.summary: Nick Bosa has gone four straight games without a sack, the first time he has done that in a season since entering the league in 2019. In the Niners' 46–40 win over Dallas he had one quarterback hit, four pressures and three penalties, two of them for jumping offside. Bosa said he cares less about the stats than he used to. "I don't think I'm playing my best football right now."

headlines.title: NFL rebukes Florio and Simms over Vrabel joke
headlines.summary: On the November 17 episode of PFT Live, Chris Simms called Patriots coach Mike Vrabel's mustache a "German mustache". Mike Florio then joked about trimming it, a thinly veiled reference to Adolf Hitler, though neither host named him. Both hosts apologised on Wednesday. The NFL's Jeff Miller called the remarks "inappropriate and offensive".
headlines.whyItMatters: It's an off-field story, but the league has publicly distanced itself from one of its primary media partners over the comments.

headlines.title: Skattebo drops the backflip after Hutchinson's injury
headlines.summary: Giants running back Cam Skattebo says he is done with his backflip celebration. It followed Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson's torn ACL, which happened when he jumped to celebrate a sack of Drake Maye in Week 10. Hutchinson has been placed on injured reserve and is out for the season.
headlines.whyItMatters: Detroit is 7–2 and second in the NFC North race, and it will need to cover the pass rush for the rest of the year without Hutchinson.

teamNews.title: Injury report: Bowers, Hemingway and others
teamNews.text: Brock Bowers did not practise on Wednesday, but Klint Kubiak says he doesn't need to practise this week to play Sunday against Denver. Tonka Hemingway (upper body) did not practise. Folorunso Fatukasi (toe) and Matt Gay (hip) were limited, and all four are listed as questionable.

teamNews.title: Mendoza's first start ends in a loss to Seattle
teamNews.text: Fernando Mendoza lost his first NFL start 21–13 to Seattle, after the Raiders scored on their opening possession. Kurt Warner said he played "too fast". Maxx Crosby said the team is "playing to win now", and power rankers didn't drop Las Vegas much.

teamNews.text: Las Vegas plays at Denver on Sunday. The Broncos are 7–2 and fifth in the AFC. Sean Payton said he could already see what Kubiak wants to build on tape. The Raiders are 4–6, ninth in the AFC and 2.0 games behind the last playoff spot.

contextCard.title: Why some NFL games are played overseas
contextCard.body: The NFL plays a small number of regular-season games outside the United States each year, including in Germany and Mexico. Teams usually spend several days abroad, which affects travel and preparation. The Patriots played in Munich this week, and the 49ers are preparing for their game in Mexico City.

nba.oneThing: The Lakers have won nine straight and are 13–2, first in the West. Quentin Grimes' 47 points and Luka Dončić's 36 carried them past Charlotte in overtime.

headlines.title: Lakers keep rolling
headlines.summary: The Lakers have won nine straight and sit at 13–2, the best record in the West. They beat Charlotte 118–114 in overtime. Quentin Grimes scored 47 with 10 threes, and Luka Dončić had 36 points, seven assists and five threes. Dončić leads the league at 38.8 points a game. Austin Reaves is still out with a heel injury and has no official timetable to return.
headlines.whyItMatters: With Reaves out, Dončić and Grimes are carrying the offence, and the run has put the Lakers clear at the top of the West standings.

headlines.title: Sixers without Maxey and Brown
headlines.summary: Tyrese Maxey was a late scratch against Orlando with right foot soreness, after warming up. Jaylen Brown is out with a left hamstring injury. Maxey averages a team-leading 26.5 points and Brown 22.6. Brown scored a season-high 31 in Monday's win over Brooklyn.
headlines.whyItMatters: Philadelphia is 12–3 and first in the East, but losing their top two scorers is a real test of their depth.

headlines.title: Towns returns to Minnesota as a champion
headlines.summary: Karl-Anthony Towns is back in Minnesota as an NBA champion. He called the visit "bittersweet" because he didn't win a title with the Wolves. Towns had 16 points, 16 rebounds and eight assists in New York's 111–102 win at Toronto, and Jalen Brunson added 31 points.
headlines.whyItMatters: New York is 8–6 and sixth in the East. The article argues the 2024 trade now clearly favours the Knicks, and they face Minnesota on Thursday.

teamNews.title: Harper ruled out against the Clippers
teamNews.text: Dylan Harper has been ruled out of Thursday's home game against the Clippers with left hip soreness. He slipped with 53 seconds left against Detroit and landed awkwardly. The Spurs are expected to give more information after medical review.
